questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Language spoken at institution, cultural richness of country, opportunities to explore nature, course selection

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was okay; we were just spammed with tonnes of information from Edinburgh University, which did make things rather complicated at times; overall, however, information could be located and used in due time

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not receive any specific assistance upon my arrival to Edinburgh; we received, again, multiple e-mails from the university, especially regarding immigration/ check-in, which was rather nice.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It was not easy; I wish that I could say the opposite, but it was a rather stressful period trying to find housing. I ended up paying quite a high rent, because I found it necessary to just get something so I would not be without a place to live once semester started. I did find a lot of use out of the platform
Spareroom.com
. I found my room through there and it worked really well!.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Just make sure you know your rights as a private tenant; Edinburgh University has produced a quick guide over these rights, which I found rather comforting.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I just had to fill out an online form with my priorities and send it as quickly as possible, as courses are granted on a first come first serve basis. This was a bit stressful, however, it was very quick and easy to fill in.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: We were able to turn to our student advisors on the CAHSS faculty. They were really helpfull towards us exchange students who did not know anything about the procedures at Edinburgh. Furthermore, when I arrived, they also really helped me with changing some of my courses.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was really successful; I got enrolled in 2 out of my 3 top priorities.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Please just be really quick to register your course wishes, when you receive an email stating that you can now enroll in courses for the semester. This way, you will be very likely to receive your preferred courses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses were rather okay; I did also choose some first-year courses, which of course were in some ways easier to follow; however, I still found some of the topics complicated and therefore really interesting to follow.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style at Edinburgh is quite similar to UCPH; we had a lot of lectures combined with seminars/ tutorials. However, I was not used to being assigned to such small classes; tutorials are special classes with only 5-10 students per class and 1 tutor, which was very new to me. However, it gave a really relaxed and informal learning environment that I really appreciated.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1) The Scottish Legal System 
2) International law – ordinary 
3) Innovations from Global South Actors

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend Scottish Legal System to all future law exchange students; It was a rather complicated and large course, however, you really get to explore and learn about a quite unique legal system and you learn to read cases from common law systems, which I found really interesting to learn.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I was not surprised by any specific costs

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Eating out/ going to pubs is not as cheap as other countries

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: tonnes of student societies from everything to rugby, wine club, debate Harry Potter etc., tutoring, lots of international student events.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: join some societies; these are great ways to meet new people, and you will be able to find at least one you like in the ocean of opportunities :))

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go explore Edinburgh city! Explore the highlands of Scotland! I want to go back next summer and explore even more of the highlands and Scottish isles; there is so much to see and do!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was really easy! the culture is very alike that in Denmark, and I really did not find any massive culture shocks at all

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: please just talk to students in your tutorial groups or societies; everyone is just trying to have fun and meet new people.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not find any particular challenging cultural differences.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I loved the pub culture! It was an amazing way to just chat and have fun with tonnes of different people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) please start looking for housing early!
2) I would recommend arriving to Edinburgh 2 weeks before terms starts as a gateway for you to get familiar with the city and maybe start some exploring!
3) don't be afraid to ask questions; we were all very confused when we arrived, however, there are a lot of people both at ECPH and UoE who will do anything in their power to help you settle in on your exchange.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: no

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: meeting new people and traveling in a different way!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: trying to make a home of an entire new city in a country I had never visited before, where I did not know anybody. However, Edinburgh did become my home, and I really miss it already!

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
